sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Orchard Park?
sections.html:
Orchard Park is a town in Erie County that contains a village of the same name, so the first job is to confirm which assessing and permit offices cover your parcel. The town spans 38.52 square miles, with the village center about 14 miles southeast of Buffalo. It was separated from Hamburg in 1850, first called Ellicott, then East Hamburgh, and took the Orchard Park name on March 1, 1934 (Wikipedia).

A sale here touches three sets of offices: the town for assessments and permits, the Erie County Clerk for the deed, and New York State for the transfer tax and disclosure forms. The town also includes hamlets such as Armor, Duells Corner, Ellicott, Loveland and Webster Corners, and Highmark Stadium sits on the western edge in the hamlet of Windom. US 219 crosses the west side of town, US 20 crosses the north, and NY 277 and NY 240 meet US 20 near the northern edge.

Families shopping for a house usually ask about schools first. The Orchard Park Central School District runs four K-5 elementary schools named Eggert, Ellicott, South Davis and Windom, plus one middle school and one high school. Naming the right elementary school in your listing or offer paperwork saves a round of questions.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about homes in Orchard Park?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counted 12,829 households in the town for 2020 to 2024 and estimated 29,804 residents on July 1, 2025. Among occupied homes, 74.5 percent are owner-occupied, the median owner-occupied value is $360,700, and median gross rent is $1,304 (QuickFacts).

  • Residents aged 65 or older: 24.5 percent
  • Median household income: $109,876 in 2024 dollars
  • Mean travel time to work: 21.5 minutes
  • Land area: 38.43 square miles, about 772 people per square mile in 2020

Stability shows in the numbers too: 91.6 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and median monthly owner costs run $2,323 with a mortgage and $910 without one.

sections.h2: Which Orchard Park offices will you deal with when you sell?
sections.html:
Three local offices matter most. The building inspector works from the Municipal Center on South Buffalo Street in the village.

  • Assessor's Office: holds your assessment, handles informal reviews and the grievance paperwork, and can be reached at 716-662-6420.
  • Building Inspector and Code Enforcement: issues permits, schedules inspections and provides zoning verification letters. The office closes for lunch from 1 PM to 2 PM Monday through Friday.
  • Town Clerk and Town Board: the board meets on the first and third Wednesdays of each month in the Municipal Building courtroom.

The town's home page also lists a stadium area rezoning presentation dated February 25, 2026 and zoning map amendments dated October 7, 2026. If your house is near the stadium or along a corridor the town is studying, ask the building office to confirm your parcel's current zoning before you set a price.

sections.h2: How do Orchard Park assessments and Grievance Day affect a sale?
sections.html:
Your assessment sets the tax a buyer will inherit, and the town's calendar decides when you can challenge it. The Assessor's Office page lists the dates below, along with a last revaluation in 1990, a uniform level of assessment of 28.5 percent and 12,412 parcels.

Assessment stepOrchard Park date
Taxable status dateMarch 1
Valuation dateJuly 1 of the previous year
Tentative rollMay 1
Grievance DayFourth Tuesday of May
Final rollJuly 1

Source: Town of Orchard Park Assessor's Office.

A level of 28.5 percent means the assessed figure on your notice is a fraction of market value, so dividing by 0.285 gives only a rough full value. The 2026 Grievance Day was May 26, and it has passed. For 2026 the town held hearings by appointment from 4 PM to 8 PM, required hearing requests and paperwork by May 19, took no electronic filings, and asked for copies of Form RP-524 for each of five Board of Assessment Review members. Ask the Assessor's Office for the 2027 details, and read the assessment review page before you file.

If your house is inside the village, ask whether the village also assesses. The state tax department says a village that assesses property needs its own separate RP-524 (tax.ny.gov).

sections.h2: What does the Erie County transfer tax cost an Orchard Park seller?
sections.html:
Erie County adds its own tax to the state tax, so an Orchard Park seller pays $4.50 for each $500 of the price, rounded up to the next $500. That total is $2.00 for New York State and $2.50 for Erie County, collected when the deed is presented for recording (Erie County Clerk fee page).

On a $360,000 sale, that is 720 units of $500, or $1,440 to the state and $1,800 to the county, for $3,240 in all. Sellers who are 62 or older and have lived in a one or two family house for at least a year can claim a senior exemption that cuts the rate to $2.00 per $500. The clerk supplies the affidavit at no charge.

Recording itself is a separate bill. For a residential deed the clerk lists a $45 statutory fee, $5 for each written side of a page, $10 to file Form TP-584 and $125 to file the RP-5217 transfer report, which makes a three-page deed $195. The state's mansion tax of 1 percent applies only at $1 million or more and falls on the buyer (tax.ny.gov).

sections.h2: Which disclosures and permits come up when selling in Orchard Park?
sections.html:
New York requires the seller of a one to four family home to complete and sign a property condition disclosure statement and deliver it before the buyer signs a binding contract (Real Property Law 462). The statute still allows as-is sale agreements. Several questions on the form line up with Orchard Park specifics:

  • Whether certificates of occupancy exist for the property
  • Whether water is municipal or from a well, and whether sewage goes to a public sewer or a septic system
  • Flood zone, drainage and past water damage
  • The school district the house sits in

The building office says work started before a permit is issued carries a double fee. Its permit list covers decks, fences, sheds, pools, roofing, furnaces and air conditioning, generators and added plumbing fixtures, and plumbing permits have been required for all plumbing work since January 2020. The town also requires owners to clear snow and ice from sidewalks along their property and says state law requires carbon monoxide detectors in every home. Fix or document these items before an inspector or a buyer finds them (building office page).

sections.h2: How does a cash offer fit an Orchard Park sale?
sections.html:
A cash offer replaces the buyer's mortgage approval and appraisal steps, which leaves title work, the transfer forms and recording as the remaining pieces of the timeline. Sellers who consider that route often want to skip showings and repairs, for example with an inherited house or a move that cannot wait for a listing cycle.

Whatever route you choose, collect your tax bill, any permits for past work, and the Erie County deed information first. Ask for the offer in writing, confirm who pays each closing cost, and have a New York attorney review the contract. The seller still signs the disclosure statement, pays the transfer tax and clears any lien before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Who pays the Erie County transfer tax when I sell in Orchard Park?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. The Erie County Clerk lists the total at $4.50 per $500 of the price, made up of $2.00 for the state and $2.50 for the county, due when the deed is presented. Owners aged 62 or older who have lived in a one or two family house for a year may qualify for the lower $2.00 rate.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Orchard Park house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. New York law lets the parties agree to an as-is sale, but the seller still has to deliver the signed property condition disclosure statement before the buyer signs the contract. Answer each question from what you actually know, and attach any inspection reports you hold.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Orchard Park?
faqs.a: The town lists Grievance Day as the fourth Tuesday of May. In 2026 that was May 26, and it has passed, so the next window opens in spring 2027. Call the Assessor's Office for the exact date, the hearing appointment deadline and the number of copies of Form RP-524 you must bring.

faqs.q: What if work on my Orchard Park house was done without a permit?
faqs.a: Talk to the building office before you list. The town says work started without a permit costs a double fee, and the disclosure form asks about certificates of occupancy. Getting the permit closed out, or disclosing the gap, is easier than reopening a contract later.

faqs.q: Where is the deed recorded after an Orchard Park sale?
faqs.a: At the Erie County Clerk, which is the county's registrar of deeds. A residential deed of three pages comes to $195 in recording charges on the clerk's schedule, and the transfer tax is paid at the same time. Title companies and attorneys normally handle the filing for you.
